title: Collector Handoff, Escrow & Rotation Playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures an operational playbook and technical spec for the "collector -> escrow -> SIEM" handoff pattern. It covers: contract surface between collectors and the escrow service, rotation/retention semantics, RBAC v2 considerations for authenticated uploads and retrievals, audit schema mapping for SIEM exports, and a set of lightweight tests and escalation steps.

Audience:
- Eng: collector owners, platform infra, SRE
- Sec/Compliance: evidentiary policy owners, auditors
- Solutions/PS: integration points for customer private deployments

High-level goals:
- Ensure each captured control artifact has an immutable chain-of-custody and signed proof envelope before archival.
- Provide a predictable, RBAC-protected upload and retrieval workflow for collectors and downstream consumers (SIEM, forensics).
- Support rotation of escrow keys and graceful re-ingest/reindex for long retention windows.
- Make SIEM export mapping explicit and reversible for audits.

Key concepts (simple):
- Collector: process that gathers event/artifact + local metadata, signs/envelopes it, and pushes to Escrow.
- Escrow (evidence-bucket-service): short-term landing area with write-only ingestion API, immutability layer and background archival to cold storage.
- Proof Envelope: JSON wrapper with metadata, collector signature, schema version, retention TTL and provenance chain.
- Verifier: service used by auditors/SIEM to validate signature and envelope integrity.

Collector -> Escrow contract (minimal):
- Transport: TLSv1.2+ with mutual TLS for dedicated customers; OAuth2 client_credentials for hosted collectors.
- Endpoint: POST /v1/ingest/proofs
- Required headers: X-Collector-Id, X-Trace-Id, X-Schema-Version, Authorization
- Body: Proof Envelope (JSON) encoded as UTF-8. Escrow returns 201 + evidence_id (UUID) and shard path.
- Idempotency: Accept Idempotency-Key header; dedup by collector-id + local-event-id.
- Max size: 10MB for initial phase. Larger uploads require multipart upload handshake (TBD in section below).

Proof Envelope (example skeleton - textual only):
{
  "schema_version": "evidence-v3",
  "collector": {"id": "collector-123", "version": "0.9.1"},
  "local_event_id": "evt-20250210-49f4",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-10T22:14:03Z",
  "artifact_type": "access-audit",
  "artifact": { /* base64 or plain JSON payload depending on type */ },
  "attachments": [ /* optional */ ],
  "provenance": [ /* chain items: collector, router, escrow */ ],
  "signature": "base64(edsig(...))",
  "retention_policy": { "ttl_days": 365, "escape_hatch": false }
}

Notes on signing:
- Collectors MUST sign the envelope using their assigned key (RBAC-v2 subject key). The escrow validates before accepting and stores the signature as part of the immutable record.
- Key format: ed25519 recommended for small payloads; RSA-2048 supported for customer-managed HSM keys.
- Rotation: collectors should support key rollover (old_key_id, new_key_id + signed link). Escrow will accept envelopes signed by previous keys for a configurable grace window (default 30 days).

RBAC v2 interactions and token model:
- Roles of interest: collector.upload, collector.admin, escrow.read, escrow.admin, siem.export, forensic.read
- Hosted environment: collectors use OAuth2 client_credentials scopes matching collector.upload. Tokens are short lived (15m) and minted by the platform auth service. Token introspection endpoint used by escrow for validating scope and subject.
- Dedicated/private: recommend mTLS + role certificate embedded in CN. For private deployments, allow HSM-backed certificates mapped to RBAC roles.
- Revocation: when a collector is deprovisioned or rotated, revoke tokens/certs via central revocation list. Escrow must check revocation list cache every 5 minutes (configurable).

Retention and escrow lifecycle:
- Ingest: evidence lands in write-only shard; immediate immutable flag set.
- Hot window: 0–30 days: full fidelity and immediate retrievals allowed to SIEM/forensics via fast path.
- Warm window: 31–365 days: evidence available via tiered retrieval API (may incur cold fetch latencies).
- Cold/Archive: >365 days: evidence moved to cold storage (long-term retention). Retrievals require restore job (48–72h) unless escrow-provisioned archive fast-path configured per customer.
- Deletion/Legal hold: evidence cannot be purged if legal_hold flag present. Deletion requests must be approved by compliance team and logged as audit events.

SIEM export mapping (principles):
- Map proof envelope -> SIEM event: generate a flattened payload with minimal PII. The SIEM pipeline is a consumer of the Verifier API rather than direct raw artifacts (preserves immutable proofs).
- Export fields (suggested): evidence_id, schema_version, collector_id, event_type, event_ts, object_summary (small hash), retention_ttl_days, confidence_bin, tags.
- Avoid storing full artifacts in primary SIEM index; instead include retrieval references (signed short-lived URLs) for deeper investigations.
- Export cadence: near-real-time for high-severity events; batched (5–15m) for low-severity bulk audits.

Operational runbook (when ingestion fails):
- 1) Collector returns 5xx/timeout: Collector retries with exponential backoff and jitter for up to 5 attempts. If still failing, write to local persistent queue and raise alert to #sec-evidence with evidence stub and trace id.
- 2) Escrow rejects with 4xx (schema/signature): Collector logs rejection with raw envelope saved locally and opens a ticket JIRA-SEC-xxx with sample. Triage by collector owner + sec-eng.
- 3) Post-ingest mismatch (verifier failure on SIEM side): SIEM must mark evidence as unverifiable and trigger forensics review. For high-severity, rollback automated actions.

Testing and verification checklist (devs/operators):
- Unit tests for envelope serialization + signing/verification.
- Integration test: collector -> escrow -> verifier -> siem simulator end-to-end on staging cluster.
- Chaos test: simulate key rotation, TTL expiry, bucket full scenarios. Ensure graceful failure modes and documented alerting.
- Sampling test harness: run evidence-synth to emit plausible artifacts at 1k/min for 24h and validate end-to-end processing and retention transitions.

Key implementation notes and TODOs (open items):
- Multipart uploads for large forensic blobs: need protocol design and progress callbacks. (Owner: Ethan)
- Escape hatch for emergency retrievals by compliance: design short-lived HMAC retrieval tokens and audit them. (Owner: Asha)
- Schema evolution: add compact summary hash to envelope to avoid SIEM ingest of heavy payloads. (Owner: Priya)
- Legal hold UI: product needs an endpoint to set/unset legal_hold per-evidence. (Req: product/console)

Escrow admin operations (playbook):
- Daily: check failed ingestion queue, reconcile with collectors, ensure revocation list synced.
- Weekly: run tombstone verification, ensure deletion pipeline honors legal holds.
- Monthly: rotate signing keys for platform services (coordinate with release engineering, announce 2 weeks in advance).

Audit artifacts to surface to auditors:
- Evidence manifest (compressed): list of evidence_id, collector_id, timestamp, signature, retention_policy.
- Key rotation log: when keys rotated, old_key_id -> new_key_id mapping and signed rollover proofs.
- Ingest SLA metrics: 95th/99th ingest latency, ingestion success rate, replay queue sizes.

Escalation matrix (quick):
- Collector ingestion errors: collector owner -> infra oncall -> sec-eng oncall
- Signature/verification mismatches: sec-eng oncall -> product compliance -> legal
- Missing evidence (customer complaint): support -> sec-eng -> infra -> legal (if required)

Appendix: sample SIEM mapping guidance (flattened JSON example, textual):
{
  "evidence_id": "uuid-...",
  "schema_version": "evidence-v3",
  "collector_id": "collector-123",
  "event_type": "access-audit",
  "event_ts": "2025-02-10T22:14:03Z",
  "summary_hash": "sha256:...",
  "retention_ttl_days": "365",
  "severiy_bin": "low",
  "artifact_ref": "/evidence/fastpath/uuid-... (signed-url)"
}

Notes to self / rough ideas: keep the verifier lightweight and co-locate near the SIEM importer to avoid repeated signature checks; but also provide a central Verifier endpoint for compliance to call directly. Consider an 'audit replay' job that can re-hydrate old envelopes and re-compute SIEM exports for retroactive investigations.

Contacts / owners:

- Asha Kapoor (compliance & audit)

Document history:

End of playbook.
